item.title: GIR PLUS celebrates 10-year milestone

item.content:encoded:
THE Get Into Rugby PLUS programme has transformed the lives of close to 10,000 children across the Pacific over the past decade, using rugby as a powerful platform to create positive social change.

Speaking during the Get Into Rugby (GIR) PLUS Awards Night at Nasau Resort and Villas in Nadi on Friday, programme patron Tihrani Uluinakauvadra reflected on the remarkable journey and achievements of the initiative since its inception 10 years ago.

Uluinakauvadra said Oceania Rugby, in partnership with UN Women and ChildFund Australia, had worked tirelessly to create safer, more inclusive and empowering environments for children and young people.

He said the programme had reached close to 10,000 children and trained more than 200 coaches across Fiji, Samoa and, most recently, Tonga.

The initiative has also been implemented in more than 80 schools and several communities throughout the Pacific.

“Through this journey, we have used rugby as a platform for positive social change,” he said.

One of the programme’s proudest moments came in 2023 when Get Into Rugby PLUS received international recognition after winning the Community Award at the prestigious Leaders Sports Awards in London.

Uluinakauvadra said the achievement reflected the programme’s contribution towards addressing social issues, breaking down barriers and creating meaningful opportunities for young people through sport.

The recognition was made even more significant by the calibre of organisations shortlisted alongside GIR PLUS, including programmes associated with the International Olympic Committee, Harvard University, the Ohio Department of Education, the National Lottery of England and the Liverpool Football Club Foundation.

“To stand among such globally recognised organisations and emerge as the winner was a proud moment,” he said.

The programme has also received recognition from researchers, with the GIR PLUS curriculum identified as one of only 55 curricula from 42 programmes across 23 countries reviewed for its contribution towards preventing Intimate Partner Violence.

Uluinakauvadra said preliminary findings from a recent programme evaluation conducted by the Nossal Institute for Global Health at the Melbourne School of Population and Global Health further reaffirmed the programme’s impact.

item.title: Trio await clearance | Bati coach keeps door open for Fainu brothers
item.description: The door remains open for the Fainu brothers. Latu, Samuela and Sione Fainu have been named in the Vodafone Fiji Bati’s 40-member extended squad for the Rugby League World Cup despite still needing to establish their Fijian heritage before they can be cleared by International Rugby League.
item.content:encoded:
The door remains open for the Fainu brothers.

Latu, Samuela and Sione Fainu have been named in the Vodafone Fiji Bati’s 40-member extended squad for the Rugby League World Cup despite still needing to establish their Fijian heritage before they can be cleared by International Rugby League.

The Wests Tigers trio have been given additional time to provide the required documentation proving their Fijian lineage.

Bati head coach Mick Potter remains hopeful the issue will be resolved before the deadline for the final 23-member squad.

“That’s still pending at the moment. We’re still waiting, so the international board will be meeting and we’re hopeful of a positive outcome,” Potter said.

The inclusion of the brothers highlights the strong influence of the Tigers in Potter’s squad.

The Tigers have several players in the extended group, including co-captain Apisai Koroisau, Jahream Bula, Sunia Turuva, Solomone Saukuru and Josese Lanyon, alongside the Fainu brothers.

Koroisau will provide vital experience and leadership, while Canterbury Bulldogs enforcer Viliame Kikau remains one of the most powerful forwards in the Bati set-up.

The squad also boasts considerable NRL and international experience, with players such as Jacob Saifiti, Kurt Donoghoe, Caleb Navale, Brandon Wakeham and Kitione Kautoga adding depth.

Former NRL stars Maika Sivo, Semi Valemei, Waqa Blake and Taane Milne further strengthen Potter’s options.

Three Fiji-based players have also earned selection in the extended squad, providing an important link to the domestic game and a pathway for local talent.

Fiji faces a daunting World Cup campaign against the Cook Islands, Australia and New Zealand.

Potter, however, is not travelling simply to make up the numbers.

“We’re not going there to lose, we are going there to win.”

For now, the Bati’s biggest selection question rests with the Fainus — and whether their Fijian story can be officially proven in time.

item.title: Suva to remain humble
item.description: GLOBAL Care Suva FC head coach Pita Rabo believes the team’s 2-1 defeat to Nasinu FC serves as an important lesson for his players to remain humble as they prepare for the semi-finals of the 2026 Extra Battle of the Giants tournament. Suva became the first team to officially secure a semi-final spot despite going down to Nasinu in their final pool match yesterday.
item.content:encoded:
GLOBAL Care Suva FC head coach Pita Rabo believes the team’s 2-1 defeat to Nasinu FC serves as an important lesson for his players to remain humble as they prepare for the semi-finals of the 2026 Extra Battle of the Giants tournament.

Suva became the first team to officially secure a semi-final spot despite going down to Nasinu in their final pool match yesterday.

The Capital side had earlier recorded convincing 3-1 victories over Navua FC and defending champions Labasa FC to establish a strong position in Group A.

Rabo said the team’s seven weeks of preparation had helped them build a competitive squad, but the loss to Nasinu was a timely reminder that they could not afford to become complacent.

“One of our biggest lessons is to humble ourselves as we go for the semi-final,” Rabo said.

“Coming out from the League and coming to BOG, we knew it would be tough. We have had a good seven weeks of preparation, building up this team, and we made sure there were some changes.”

Rabo said Suva’s strong start to the tournament had given the team confidence, but they now needed to focus on improving as they moved closer to the knockout stage.

“We came into the tournament having big wins, and now we start to move in the right direction,” he said.

item.title: Vasu takes charge | High-performance specialist returns home for Drua role
item.description: LUKE Vasu has been handed one of the Drua’s toughest jobs — turning Fiji’s natural athleticism into the physical strength and durability needed to compete with the best in Super Rugby Pacific. The Suvavou-born performance specialist returns home with experience across Australia, New Zealand and Japan, bringing with him a high-performance background that could change how the Swire Shipping Fijian D
item.content:encoded:
LUKE Vasu has been handed one of the Drua’s toughest jobs — turning Fiji’s natural athleticism into the physical strength and durability needed to compete with the best in Super Rugby Pacific.

The Suvavou-born performance specialist returns home with experience across Australia, New Zealand and Japan, bringing with him a high-performance background that could change how the Swire Shipping Fijian Drua prepare for the demands of professional rugby.

Appointed Head of Athletic Performance ahead of the 2027 Shop N Save Super Rugby Pacific season, Vasu will oversee the physical preparation and development of the franchise’s players.

His experience spans the NSW Waratahs in Australia, Hurricanes Poua and provincial rugby in New Zealand, and Toyota Industries Shuttles in Japan.

That journey has exposed him to different approaches to strength and conditioning, speed development, workload management, GPS monitoring, recovery and rehabilitation.

Now comes the bigger test – adapting those lessons to the Drua.

Super Rugby Pacific is a brutal examination of a player’s body. The speed, contact, travel and intensity leave little room for poor preparation.

For the Drua to make the next step, talent alone will not be enough.

Players must be able to reproduce their best performances week after week.

That is where Vasu’s role becomes critical.

His challenge will not simply be to make players bigger or stronger. It will be to build a performance system that improves durability, recovery and consistency while allowing Fijian players to retain the speed and flair that make them dangerous.

His experience overseas could provide the missing link between natural ability and sustained performance.

Vasu has seen first-hand how professional teams use science, data and structured preparation to get more from their athletes.

Now he has the chance to bring that knowledge home.

“I am truly excited and grateful for the opportunity to join the Drua vuvale,” Vasu said.

For Vasu, the appointment is a homecoming.

For the Drua, it could be the beginning of a harder, smarter and more professional approach to physical performance.

Build a team that can still run hard, hit hard and finish strong when others begin to fade.

item.title: Politini backs new faces
item.description: THE McDonald’s Nadi senior men’s rugby coach Cohan Politini says his side’s 31-12 victory over Navosa has provided another valuable opportunity to test the depth of the squad and give new players a chance to prove themselves. Nadi defeated Navosa in round six of the Skipper Cup competition at King Charles Park in Nadi on Saturday, with three more players making their debuts for the home side.
item.content:encoded:
THE McDonald’s Nadi senior men’s rugby coach Cohan Politini says his side’s 31-12 victory over Navosa has provided another valuable opportunity to test the depth of the squad and give new players a chance to prove themselves.

Nadi defeated Navosa in round six of the Skipper Cup competition at King Charles Park in Nadi on Saturday, with three more players making their debuts for the home side.

Politini said the coaching staff continued to rotate players and used the recent matches to develop new talent ahead of the tougher contests later in the competition.

“We had three debutants this week again, so altogether from last week we had seven new faces, and we had 10 new guys altogether on the field against Navosa,” Politini said.

“We are happy that we could use this game to believe in all these new players.”

Nadi had anticipated a strong response from Navosa following their disappointing defeat last week and Politini said his players prepared accordingly.

“We were anticipating Navosa to bounce back after that disappointing defeat last week, and bounce back they did today.

“But we ensured that we covered all those areas during last week, and we had a very good week of preparation for them.”

The match also marked the return of Fiji 7s player Nacani Boginisoko, who is gradually making his way back into the Nadi setup after recovering from injury.

Politini said the coaching staff was taking a cautious approach with the talented back.

“We are happy to have another back. He played a lot of games for Nadi last year, but he has come back from an injury.

“We are just bringing him along slowly and hopefully we can use him more in the next few games.”

Politini said Nadi had deliberately rested several senior players in recent weeks, allowing emerging players to gain valuable experience.

However, he expects more experienced campaigners to return as the competition enters a crucial stage.

item.title: Rewa rolls past Ba
item.description: REWA FC moved to the top of Group B after producing a dominant performance to defeat Dayals Steels Ba FC 3-0 in their second pool match of the Extra Battle of the Giants tournament at 4R Stadium, Govind Park on Saturday night. The victory strengthened Rewa’s position in the race for a semi-final spot, while Ba will now need a positive result in their remaining match to keep their hopes alive.
item.content:encoded:
REWA FC moved to the top of Group B after producing a dominant performance to defeat Dayals Steels Ba FC 3-0 in their second pool match of the Extra Battle of the Giants tournament at 4R Stadium, Govind Park on Saturday night.

The victory strengthened Rewa’s position in the race for a semi-final spot, while Ba will now need a positive result in their remaining match to keep their hopes alive.

Rewa took the lead in the 40th minute through Brazilian import Lucas, who beat five Ba defenders before calmly placing the ball into the corner of the net.

Rewa went into halftime with a 1-0 advantage.

The side continued to control possession in the second half and extended its lead through Merrill Nand before Ivan Kumar added the third goal to seal a convincing victory.

Ba coach Ravinesh Kumar admitted his side was second best on the day and was punished for lapses in concentration.

“It was not our day. Rewa was the best team. We lost concentration on three occasions and that cost us three goals,” Kumar said.

Rewa coach-player Tevita Waranivalu said his team’s main objective was to secure the three points.

“We had a plan and we stuck to the plan. We really controlled the game in the second half,” Waranivalu said.

item.title: Values first at Junior Kaji festival
item.description: THE Nadi Junior Kaji Rugby Festival is continuing to play a crucial role in developing the next generation of rugby players in Nadi, with values taking priority over winning. Nadi Rugby Union operations manager Jeff Tamata said the festival had been running for the past seven years and was designed to ensure young players were properly grounded in the principles of the game.
item.content:encoded:
THE Nadi Junior Kaji Rugby Festival is continuing to play a crucial role in developing the next generation of rugby players in Nadi, with values taking priority over winning.

Nadi Rugby Union operations manager Jeff Tamata said the festival had been running for the past seven years and was designed to ensure young players were properly grounded in the principles of the game.

The two-day festival, held on Wednesday and Thursday, bringing together young players from rugby clubs throughout Nadi.

Of the 13 clubs under the Nadi Rugby Union, 11 are taking part in the rugby festival, involving boys and girls from the under-8, U10, U12, U14, U16 and U18 grades.

Tamata said the festival was deliberately structured differently from highly competitive tournaments.

“The values of rugby are the priority,” he said.

“We take the competitive mindset away from them and build into them the values of rugby.”

Those values are reflected in the DRIPS philosophy – discipline, respect, integrity, patience and solidarity.

Tamata said the festival had grown significantly since its humble beginnings seven years ago when only three clubs participated.

He believes the programme has become an important pathway for grassroots rugby development in Nadi, particularly because it reaches young people beyond the traditional school rugby system.

“These are clubs, not schools,” Tamata said.

He explained that the club structure allowed organisers to bring in young people who may not be attending school, while also creating opportunities for students from schools that do not traditionally have rugby programmes.

Girls’ participation is also a major requirement, with clubs expected to include female teams in their categories.

Tamata said the union was equally strict on compliance, with two established clubs missing the current second-term holiday festival because they failed to meet the required standards.

He said building discipline and strong character at a young age would make it easier for players to adapt to the culture and expectations of higher-level rugby.

For Nadi Rugby Union, the festival is about much more than producing winning teams – it is about producing better players and better people.

item.title: Kadavu laments halftime lead
item.description: KADAVU’S strong first-half effort was not enough to secure victory as Suva fought back to beat the island side 19-10 in round six of the Subrails Marama Cup competition at Suva Grammar School on Saturday. Kadavu went into halftime break with a 10-7 advantage after putting Suva under pressure in the opening 40 minutes.
item.content:encoded:
KADAVU’S strong first-half effort was not enough to secure victory as Suva fought back to beat the island side 19-10 in round six of the Subrails Marama Cup competition at Suva Grammar School on Saturday.

Kadavu went into halftime break with a 10-7 advantage after putting Suva under pressure in the opening 40 minutes.

However, the home side responded strongly after the break, scoring two unanswered tries while keeping Kadavu scoreless to complete the comeback.

The defeat comes after Kadavu produced an impressive performance in round five, beating Lautoka 41-15 at Churchill Park.

Kadavu coach Etuate Nauro had previously spoken about the difficulties faced by the side, including persistent rain and limited access to suitable training facilities in Kadavu.

“We came through after a lot of challenges and struggles back in Kadavu,” Nauro said.

“The weather was rainy, we couldn’t find a good ground to train on.”

Despite those setbacks, Nauro credited his players for their commitment to the campaign.

“We thank the girls for all the effort they have shown us,” he said.

Captain Ulumila Likubai has also highlighted the significance of representing Kadavu, particularly during the team’s historic home match against Rewa.
